Check that grafted taxa and missing clades respect their grafting constraints

Source: R/check_grafting_constraints.R
check_grafting_constraints.Rd

This function checks, a posteriori, that each taxon grafted on a phylogeny sits in a valid position. For missing taxa grafted with graft_missing_taxa(): within its target clade (or on its stem branch if allowed), and outside its excluded subclades. For missing clades grafted with graft_missing_clades(): each missing clade (the taxa sharing the same sister clade) must form one clade, grafted on the stem branch of its sister clade.

The type of grafting is detected from missing_taxa_list: a $Target_clade item for taxa, a $Sister_clade item for missing clades (see 'Missing clades' in Details section). With a simmap, the validity of the states of the taxa or of the missing clades are checked too.

The function can also check that the backbone phylogeny is preserved by the grafting once the grafted taxa are pruned.

Usage

check_grafting_constraints(
  phy_grafted,
  phy_backbone,
  missing_taxa_list,
  include_target_clade_stem = TRUE,
  use_excluded_subclades = TRUE,
  exclude_subclades_stem = TRUE,
  allowed_states = NULL,
  treat_states_as_ranges = FALSE,
  check_backbone = TRUE,
  tolerance = 1e-06,
  stop_on_failure = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

phy_grafted

An object of class "phylo". The phylogeny after grafting. It can also be a set of grafted phylogenies (class "multiPhylo", from nb_simulations > 1), or a list with one element per stochastic map (a "phylo" or a "multiPhylo", from the grafting functions used with a "multiSimmap" to account for multiple alternative trait evolutionary histories). See 'Several grafted phylogenies' in Details section.

phy_backbone

An object of class "phylo". The backbone phylogeny used for grafting (i.e., before grafting).

missing_taxa_list

A list with the information on the grafted taxa. Typically the same list as used for grafting. Items: $Taxon_name, $Target_clade (taxa grafted with phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()) or $Sister_clade (missing clades grafted with phylograftR::graft_missing_clades()), and optionally $include_target_clade_stem, $Excluded_subclades and $exclude_subclades_stem (taxa only), and $allowed_states. Exactly one of $Target_clade and $Sister_clade must be provided: it defines the type of the check. Every item provided must be named after $Taxon_name (same names, same order), as in the grafting functions, see these functions for details.

It can also be the list of both types of lineages to graft, list(taxa = ..., clades = ...), as returned by phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list() when both types are provided, to check the output of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(). Each part is then checked on the same phylogenies and the output is a named list (see 'Value'). In a missing clade, tips grafted as missing taxa, during the other grafting step, are tolerated: when the missing clades are grafted first, taxa can be grafted within them afterwards.

include_target_clade_stem

Logical. Same as in phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa(): whether grafting on the stem branch of target clades is accepted. Taxa with a value in missing_taxa_list$include_target_clade_stem use it instead (NA or no item: this global value is used). Ignored for missing clades. Default is TRUE.

use_excluded_subclades

Logical. Same as in phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa(): whether to check the excluded subclades. If no $Excluded_subclades item is found in missing_taxa_list, a warning is issued and excluded subclades are not checked. Ignored for missing clades. Default is TRUE.

exclude_subclades_stem

Logical. Same as in phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa(): whether the stem of the excluded subclades is also excluded (a taxon sister to an excluded subclade is then a violation). Excluded subclades with a value in missing_taxa_list$exclude_subclades_stem use it instead (NA or no item: this global value is used). Ignored for missing clades. Default is TRUE.

allowed_states

Character vector. Same as in phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa(): the states in which grafting is allowed. This is the default for all taxa: taxa with a value in missing_taxa_list$allowed_states use this specific value instead. Only used if phy_grafted has a $simmap item (the updated simmap returned by phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() with a simmap). If the $simmap item is a list of the simmaps of several traits (grafting constrained with several traits), allowed_states is a list with one element per trait (in the order of the traits, or named after the traits; NULL = all the states of the trait, or any range for the trait treated as ranges), and the taxon-level values of missing_taxa_list$allowed_states are given per trait as in the grafting functions (see 'Several traits' in Details). The function stops if some states are not in the simmap. Default is NULL (all states allowed for the taxa without a taxon-level value).

treat_states_as_ranges

Logical. Same as in phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa(): whether the states of the simmap and the allowed states are treated as biogeographic ranges: an allowed range enables grafting on branch pieces in any range that contains it: "A" can be grafted on "A", "AB" and "ABC", whereas "AB" can be grafted on "AB" and "ABC" but not "A". Only used if phy_grafted has a $simmap item, otherwise the function stops if TRUE. With a $simmap item that is a list of the simmaps of several traits, takes a logical vector with one value per trait, with at most one TRUE to identify the trait treated as ranges (positional, or named after the traits in any order, as in the grafting functions; a single FALSE is accepted, a single TRUE stops). States / ranges are coded as in BioGeoBEARS (see the Details section "Biogeographic ranges as states"). The function stops if the states of the simmap or the allowed states are not correctly coded, or if an area of the allowed states is not in the simmap. Default is FALSE (states are matched exactly).

check_backbone

Logical. Whether to check that the topology and branch lengths of the backbone are preserved once the grafted taxa are pruned. Default is TRUE.

tolerance

Numeric. Tolerance for the maximum deviation in backbone branch lengths, relative to the depth (root age) of the backbone. Default is 1e-6.

stop_on_failure

Logical. Whether to stop with an error if any constraint is violated. Default is FALSE.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print a summary of the checks. Default is TRUE.

Value

The structure of the output depends on the type of elements grafted, and their associated grafting function used in the process.

Missing taxa. With a $Target_clade list (for missing taxa), the function assumed that phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() was used for the grafting. It returns a data.frame with one row per taxon in missing_taxa_list (in the original order) for each phylogeny checked, and the following columns:

  • $map: Name of the stochastic map used to constrain grafting based on species attributes. NA if none was used.

  • $simulation: Integer. Index of the simulation (the index in the name "sim_k" of the phylogeny; 1 for a single phylogeny).

  • $seed: Integer. Seed of the simulation (attribute "seed" of the phylogeny, NA if unknown).

  • $Taxon_name: Name of the taxon.

  • $in_tree: Logical. Whether the taxon is found in the grafted phylogeny.

  • $include_target_clade_stem: Logical. Whether the stem of the target clade was accepted for this taxon (missing_taxa_list$include_target_clade_stem of the taxon if provided, otherwise the global include_target_clade_stem argument).

  • $target_position: Character string. Position of the taxon relative to its target clade: "crown" (within the clade), "stem" (sister to the clade, or to other missing taxa grafted on the stem), "tip_branch" (on the branch of the tip, for single-tip target clades), or "outside" (neither within the clade nor on its stem = an error).

  • $target_ok: Logical. Whether the position respects the target clade ("crown" or, if the stem is accepted for the taxon, "stem"; "tip_branch" for single-tip clades).

  • $excluded_ok: Logical. Whether the taxon is outside all its excluded subclades (and not on their stem, for the subclades with an excluded stem).

  • $n_excluded_violated: Integer. Number of excluded subclades violated.

  • $excluded_violated: Character string. Names of the excluded subclades violated (or their indices if the subclades are not named), separated by commas (NA if none).

  • $states_ok: Logical. Only checked if phy_grafted has a $simmap item: whether the taxon was grafted in one of its allowed states (missing_taxa_list$allowed_states of the taxon if provided, otherwise the global allowed_states argument; all the states if neither is provided). With treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE, the state of the terminal branch of the taxon (the range it inherited) must be one of its allowed ranges (any range if the taxon has no allowed states). NA if phy_grafted has no $simmap. With the maps of several traits, TRUE if the taxon was grafted in an allowed state for all the traits.

  • $states_ok_<trait>: Logical. Only with the maps of several traits (one column per trait, named after the traits): whether the taxon was grafted in one of its allowed states for this trait. Used to find which trait is violated when $states_ok is FALSE.

  • $ranges_ok: Logical. Only checked with treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE (or a range trait with several traits) and a $simmap item: whether the range inherited by the taxon is contained in the state of the lineage at the graft point (see the Details section "Biogeographic ranges as states"). NA if not checked, or if the taxon is grafted at the root (no parent lineage). This differs from $states_ok that checks only the validity of the terminal tip state. Here, the validity of the inherited range is assessed against the range of the backbone lineage it was grafted on.

  • $ok: Logical. Whether the taxon respects its target clade, its excluded subclades, and its allowed states and ranges (if checked).

Missing clades. With a $Sister_clade list (for missing clades), the function assumed that phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() was used for the grafting. It returns a data.frame with one row per missing clade, i.e., per group of taxa sharing the same sister clade, numbered in the order of their first appearance in missing_taxa_list, for each phylogeny checked.

The columns $map, $simulation and $seed are the same as above, followed by:

  • $missing_clade: ID or label of the missing clade: the label of its sister clade if missing_taxa_list has a $Sister_clade_name item (character string), otherwise the ID of the clade (integer).

  • $Taxon_names: Character string. The taxa of the missing clade, separated by commas.

  • $n_taxa: Integer. Number of taxa of the missing clade.

  • $Sister_clade_tips: Character string. The tips that define the sister clade, separated by commas.

  • $in_tree: Logical. Whether all the taxa of the missing clade are found in the grafted phylogeny. $n_in_tree is the number of taxa found.

  • $monophyletic: Logical. Whether the taxa form one clade of the grafted phylogeny with no other tip (backbone tip or taxon of another missing clade).

  • $sister_position: Character string. Position of the missing clade relative to its sister clade: "stem" (sister to the clade, or to other missing taxa grafted on its stem, with no other backbone tip in between), "tip_branch" (on the branch of the tip, for a single-tip sister clade), "crown" (nested within the sister clade), or "outside".

  • $sister_ok: Logical. Whether the missing clade is on the stem of its sister clade ("stem" or "tip_branch").

  • $states_ok: Logical. Only checked if phy_grafted has a $simmap item: whether the whole missing clade (its stem branch and all its descendant branches) is in one single state, and this state is allowed (missing_taxa_list$allowed_states if provided, otherwise the global allowed_states argument; all the states if neither is provided). NA if phy_grafted has no $simmap. With the maps of several traits, TRUE if this is the case for all the traits, and $states_ok_<trait> gives the result of each trait. With treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE, the single state is the range inherited by the missing clade, which must be one of its allowed ranges (any range if none).

  • $ranges_ok: Logical. Only checked with treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE (or a range trait): whether the range inherited by the missing clade is contained in the state of the lineage at the graft point.

  • $ok: Logical. Whether the missing clade is in the tree, monophyletic, on the stem of its sister clade, and in an allowed state and range (if checked).

With a list(taxa, clades) covering both types of missing lineages, the output is a named list with the elements taxa and clades**, each element contains the output of its type (as described above), with the overarching attribute "all_ok" (TRUE if all the constraints are respected for both types of grafted lineages).

Multiple maps. With a list of maps as phy_grafted, the function returns a list of such data.frames (one per map, named after the maps, with the attribute "all_ok" for all the maps), since the maps have their own constraints: in each data.frame, the rows of all the simulations of the map are merged.

The data.frame has the following attributes (for several phylogenies: "topology_preserved" and "backbone_preserved" are TRUE if they are TRUE for all the phylogenies, the deviations are the maximum over the phylogenies, and "all_ok" is TRUE if it is TRUE for all of them):

  • "topology_preserved": Logical. Whether the backbone topology is preserved once the grafted taxa are pruned (NA if check_backbone = FALSE).

  • "max_branch_length_deviation": Numeric. Maximum absolute deviation in backbone branch lengths (NA if the topology is not preserved).

  • "max_branch_length_deviation_relative": Numeric. Same, relative to the depth of the backbone.

  • "backbone_preserved": Logical. Whether both topology and branch lengths are preserved, within tolerance (NA if check_backbone = FALSE).

  • "all_ok": Logical. Whether all taxa respect their constraints and the backbone is preserved (if checked).

  • "trait_names": Character vector. Names of the traits checked (only with the maps of several traits, otherwise NULL).

  • "range_trait": Character string. Name of the trait treated as ranges (only with the maps of several traits, otherwise NULL).

  • "phylogenies": data.frame with one row per phylogeny checked (columns map, simulation, seed, n_failed (number of taxa, or of missing clades, that failed), backbone_preserved and all_ok).

Attributes are accessed with attr(x = output, which = "attribute_name").

Details

Missing taxa

A taxon respects its target clade if it is found within the clade, or on its stem branch if the stem is accepted for this taxon: global include_target_clade_stem = TRUE, or missing_taxa_list$include_target_clade_stem of this taxon (the taxon is then sister to the target clade, or to other missing taxa sister to the target clade, with no other backbone tip in between). For a single-tip target clade, the taxon must be on the branch of the tip, with no other backbone tip in between.

The 'stem' position is not restricted to a taxon being directly sister to the target clade: taxa grafted on the stem can receive further grafts, so several missing taxa can form together a group sister to the target clade (i.e, a missing-only subtree grafted on the the stem). Only backbone tips are considered when checking the position of a taxon (missing taxa are ignored), so such configurations are valid.

If phy_grafted has a $simmap item (the updated simmap returned by the grafting functions when a simmap is provided), the states are also checked: a grafted taxon is in the state of the point where it was grafted, along its whole terminal branch, so the states of its terminal branch in the simmap must be allowed. The simmap item is used as it is: it is not compared to the backbone.

A taxon respects its excluded subclades if it is not nested within any of them. If the stem of an excluded subclade is excluded (exclude_subclades_stem = TRUE, the default), the taxon must also not be on its stem, i.e., sister to the subclade (or to other missing taxa sister to the subclade), with no other backbone tip in between. For a single-tip excluded subclade, the taxon must not be on the branch of the tip. As in phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa(), if the stem of the subclade is not excluded, the taxon can be sister to the subclade, not within it.

Branches of the backbone are matched between the pruned grafted phylogeny and the backbone by the set of tips they subtend. Branch lengths are considered preserved if the maximum deviation, relative to the depth of the backbone, is lower than tolerance.

Missing clades

graft_missing_clades() grafts the taxa sharing the same sister clade together, as one missing clade, on the stem branch of their sister clade. With a $Sister_clade list, this function checks each missing clade (the taxa whose sister clades have the same backbone tips, whatever the pair of tips used to define them) for:

  • its presence ($in_tree): all its taxa must be in the grafted phylogeny ;

  • its monophyly ($monophyletic): its taxa must form one clade of the grafted phylogeny, free of any other tip ;

  • its position ($sister_position and $sister_ok): the missing clade must be sister to its sister clade, or to other missing taxa grafted on the same stem, with no other backbone tip in between ("stem"), or on the terminal branch of a single-tip sister clade ("tip_branch"). A missing clade nested within its sister clade ("crown") is a violation, unlike a taxon grafted by graft_missing_taxa() within its target clade;

  • with a $simmap item, its states ($states_ok): the whole missing clade is in the state of the point where it was grafted, so its stem branch and all its descendant branches must have one single state, which must be allowed. The taxa of a missing clade are grafted together, so they must share their allowed states (the function stops otherwise, as the grafting function does). With treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE, the whole missing clade inherits one range, which must be contained in the state of the lineage at the graft point (see 'Biogeographic ranges as states').

*e arguments include_target_clade_stem, use_excluded_subclades and exclude_subclades_stem only apply to taxa and are ignored. The backbone is checked as for taxa. Several phylogenies, maps and traits are handled as described in the corresponding sections. With verbose = TRUE, the summary counts missing clades instead of taxa.

Several traits

If the grafting used several traits as constraints, the grafting functions return a $simmap item that is a list of simmaps, one per trait, named after the traits, (or "trait_1", "trait_2", ... if the input was not named). Then this function checks the validity of states trait by trait: the states of the terminal branch of the taxon in the simmap of each trait must be allowed for this trait. The allowed states of each taxon and trait are resolved as in the grafting functions: the value of missing_taxa_list$allowed_states for this trait if provided, otherwise the global allowed_states for this trait, otherwise all the states of the trait (see phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()). $states_ok_<trait> gives the result for each trait, and $states_ok is TRUE only if all traits are ok. With verbose = TRUE, the number of violations is also given for each trait.

With a trait treated as ranges (treat_states_as_ranges, one TRUE in the vector), the checks of 'Biogeographic ranges as states' are performed on this trait: $states_ok_<trait> is TRUE if the range inherited is one of the allowed ranges (any range if the taxon has no allowed ranges), and $ranges_ok is TRUE if the range inherited is contained in the state of the lineage of this trait at the graft point. The other traits are checked as exact matches. The attribute "range_trait" gives the name of the range trait.

Several grafted phylogenies

The phylogenies are checked one by one against the same phy_backbone and missing_taxa_list. When allowed_states or treat_states_as_ranges are used, each phylogeny is checked with its own $simmap item (the maps of a "multiSimmap" can differ). The warnings about the inputs are sent once. With several phylogenies, verbose = TRUE prints one summary for all of them (number of phylogenies respecting all the constraints, number of violations of each type, and the first phylogenies with violations), and stop_on_failure = TRUE stops if any phylogeny violates a constraint.

Biogeographic ranges as states

With treat_states_as_ranges = TRUE, the states are biogeographic ranges (one capital letter per area, e.g., "A", "AB", "BC"), and a range is a set of areas. A grafted lineage inherits one of its allowed ranges, which can be a subset of the state of the lineage it is grafted on. Example: the range "A" can be inherited from a lineage in the state "AB". This then describes a subset sympatric speciation event: (AB) -> (AB), (A).

Two checks are then performed:

  • $states_ok: the state of the terminal branch of the taxon is exactly one of its allowed ranges (the range inherited).

  • $ranges_ok: the range inherited is contained in the state of the lineage at the graft point (e.g., "A" is contained in "AB", but "BC" is not). The check is skipped (NA) for taxa grafted at the root.

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::check_grafting_plan() to check a priori the feasibility of a grafting plan, before grafting.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa based on target clades and excluded subclades.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() to graft groups of missing taxa as sister clades of backbone clades.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa_and_clades() to graft missing taxa and missing clades in one run, with a single set of inputs.

  • phylograftR::extract_grafting_info() to extract a posteriori information on the location of grafted lineages.

  • phylograftR::extract_sampling_info() to extract a posteriori the richness and the sampling fraction of the clades in each grafted phylogeny.

  • phylograftR::extract_BD_model_summary() to extract a posteriori information on the birth-death models fitted during grafting.

Author

Maël Doré

Examples

# --- Prepare data --- #

# Create a toy backbone phylogeny: ultrametric, with a root age of 50 time units
set.seed(1234)
phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30)
phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50

# List the missing taxa to graft
missing_taxa_list <- list(
  Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"),
  # Items are named after Taxon_name (same names, same order)
  Target_clade = list(X1 = c("t26", "t18"), X2 = c("t8", "t22"), X3 = "t5", X4 = c("t26", "t18")),
  Excluded_subclades = list(X1 = list(c("t10", "t19")), X2 = NULL, X3 = NULL, X4 = NULL))

# --- Perform grafting of missing taxa--- #

# Graft the missing taxa with graft_missing_taxa()
grafted_phy <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,
                                  verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# --- Check one grafted phylogenies --- #

# Check that the grafted taxa respect their constraints, and that the backbone is preserved
check_results <- check_grafting_constraints(phy_grafted = grafted_phy, phy_backbone = phy,
                                            missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list)
#> 4 taxa checked
#>   - Missing from the grafted tree: 0
#>   - Target clade violated:          0
#>   - Excluded subclade violated:     0
#>   - Backbone: topology preserved, branch lengths shifted by max 4.82e-09 (9.65e-11 of backbone depth; tolerance = 1e-06)
#>   => All constraints respected
# Inspect results
check_results
#>     map simulation seed Taxon_name in_tree include_target_clade_stem
#> X1 <NA>          1 1234         X1    TRUE                      TRUE
#> X2 <NA>          1 1234         X2    TRUE                      TRUE
#> X3 <NA>          1 1234         X3    TRUE                      TRUE
#> X4 <NA>          1 1234         X4    TRUE                      TRUE
#>    target_position target_ok excluded_ok n_excluded_violated excluded_violated
#> X1           crown      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA
#> X2           crown      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA
#> X3      tip_branch      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA
#> X4           crown      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA
#>    states_ok ranges_ok   ok
#> X1        NA        NA TRUE
#> X2        NA        NA TRUE
#> X3        NA        NA TRUE
#> X4        NA        NA TRUE
# Check overall results
attr(check_results, "all_ok")
#> [1] TRUE

# --- Check several grafted phylogenies --- #

# Build 3 grafted phylognies (i.e., simulations) with the same backbone and constraints
grafted_phys <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,
                                   nb_simulations = 3, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# Check all resulting grafted phylogenies at once
check_results_multi <- check_grafting_constraints(phy_grafted = grafted_phys, phy_backbone = phy,
                                                  missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list)
#> 3 phylogenies checked (no map), 4 taxa each
#>   - Phylogenies respecting all the constraints: 3/3
#>   Violations, over all the phylogenies (number of taxa x phylogenies):
#>   - Missing from the grafted tree: 0
#>   - Target clade violated:          0
#>   - Excluded subclade violated:     0
#>   - Backbone: preserved in 3/3 phylogenies, branch lengths shifted by max 9.65e-11 of backbone depth (tolerance = 1e-06)
#>   => All constraints respected

# With several simulations: the data.frame has the columns 'map', 'simulation' and 'seed',
# and the summary is printed once for all the phylogenies
head(check_results_multi[, c("map", "simulation", "seed", "Taxon_name", "ok")])
#>    map simulation      seed Taxon_name   ok
#> 1 <NA>          1      1234         X1 TRUE
#> 2 <NA>          1      1234         X2 TRUE
#> 3 <NA>          1      1234         X3 TRUE
#> 4 <NA>          1      1234         X4 TRUE
#> 5 <NA>          2 488349520         X1 TRUE
#> 6 <NA>          2 488349520         X2 TRUE

# An additional attribute provide a summary per phylogeny:
# number of taxa that failed, backbone preserved, all constraints respected
attr(check_results_multi, "phylogenies")
#>    map simulation      seed n_failed backbone_preserved all_ok
#> 1 <NA>          1      1234        0               TRUE   TRUE
#> 2 <NA>          2 488349520        0               TRUE   TRUE
#> 3 <NA>          3 469344150        0               TRUE   TRUE


# --- Check missing clades grafted with graft_missing_clades() --- #

# With a 'Sister_clade' item, the missing clades are checked (one row per missing clade)

# Prepare a missing_taxa_list for missing clades
missing_clades_list <- list(
  Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2", "M3"),
  Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t26", "t18"), M2 = c("t26", "t18"), M3 = "t5"))

# Graft the missing clades with graft_missing_clades()
grafted_clades <- graft_missing_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,
                                       verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# Check results
check_clades <- check_grafting_constraints(phy_grafted = grafted_clades, phy_backbone = phy,
                                           missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list)
#> 2 missing clades (3 taxa) checked
#>   - Missing from the grafted tree:        0
#>   - Not forming one clade:                0
#>   - Not sister to their sister clade:     0
#>   - Backbone: topology preserved, branch lengths shifted by max 4.82e-09 (9.65e-11 of backbone depth; tolerance = 1e-06)
#>   => All constraints respected
# Inspect results
check_clades[, c("missing_clade", "Taxon_names", "monophyletic", "sister_position", "ok")]
#>   missing_clade Taxon_names monophyletic sister_position   ok
#> 1             1      M1, M2         TRUE            stem TRUE
#> 2             2          M3         TRUE      tip_branch TRUE


# --- Check the constraints from several traits, with biogeographic ranges --- #

# With the stochastic maps of several traits used to assign grafting constraints,
# 'allowed_states' has one element per trait,
# and 'treat_states_as_ranges' is a logical vector with one value per trait
# used to identify which trait was treated as biogeographic ranges.

# Load datasets
data(toy_backbone)
data(toy_simmap_ranges)
data(toy_simmap_elevation)
data(toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation)

# Graft phylogeny using elevation and biogeographic ranges as constraints
grafted_phy_traits <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = toy_backbone,
    missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation,
    simmap = list(biogeo = toy_simmap_ranges, elevation = toy_simmap_elevation),
    allowed_states = list(c("A", "B"), NULL),
    treat_states_as_ranges = c(biogeo = TRUE, elevation = FALSE),
    verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# The result has the joint columns 'states_ok' and 'ranges_ok' (ranges of the 'range trait'),
# and the column 'states_ok_<trait>' for each trait. The summary details the failures per trait.
check_traits <- check_grafting_constraints(
    phy_grafted = grafted_phy_traits,
    phy_backbone = toy_backbone,
    missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation,
    allowed_states = list(c("A", "B"), NULL),
    treat_states_as_ranges = c(biogeo = TRUE, elevation = FALSE))
#> 7 taxa checked
#>   - Missing from the grafted tree: 0
#>   - Target clade violated:          0
#>   - Excluded subclade violated:     0
#>   - Allowed states violated:        0 (biogeo: 0, elevation: 0)
#>   - Range not in graft-point state: 0
#>   - Backbone: topology preserved, branch lengths shifted by max 4.53e-09 (9.06e-11 of backbone depth; tolerance = 1e-06)
#>   => All constraints respected
check_traits[, c("Taxon_name", "states_ok", "states_ok_biogeo", "states_ok_elevation",
                 "ranges_ok", "ok")]
#>         Taxon_name states_ok states_ok_biogeo states_ok_elevation ranges_ok
#> New_sp1    New_sp1      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE
#> New_sp2    New_sp2      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE
#> New_sp3    New_sp3      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE
#> New_sp4    New_sp4      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE
#> New_sp5    New_sp5      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE
#> New_sp6    New_sp6      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE
#> New_sp7    New_sp7      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE
#>           ok
#> New_sp1 TRUE
#> New_sp2 TRUE
#> New_sp3 TRUE
#> New_sp4 TRUE
#> New_sp5 TRUE
#> New_sp6 TRUE
#> New_sp7 TRUE

# --- Check both types of missing lineages grafted in one run --- #

# With list(taxa, clades), both parts are checked on the same phylogenies
both_list <- list(
  taxa = missing_taxa_list,
  clades = list(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2"), Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t8", "t22"), M2 = "t5")))

grafted_both <- graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = both_list,
                                              verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

checks_both <- check_grafting_constraints(phy_grafted = grafted_both, phy_backbone = phy,
                                          missing_taxa_list = both_list, verbose = FALSE)
names(checks_both)
#> [1] "taxa"   "clades"
attr(checks_both, "all_ok") # "all_ok" is TRUE if both types of missing lineages are ok
#> [1] TRUE
